clue.text: Tripe and cobblers: prep's done for King Charles's dinner?

definitions.text: Tripe and cobblers: prep's done for King Charles's dinner?

parts.words: Tripe and cobblers: prep's done for King Charles's dinner?
parts.note: tripe and cobblers are British slang for nonsense

explanation.surface: A dog-owner's menu: offal and pies, with the cooking done for a royal's evening meal.
explanation.walkthrough: King Charles is not the monarch but a breed of spaniel; prep is British school slang for homework, and tripe and cobblers both mean rubbish, so the whole thing is the classic lame excuse.
explanation.definitionFit: The stock schoolchild's excuse is proverbially nonsense, and it blames the family pet for eating the unfinished assignment.

clue.text: What would be funny, doubling up about long laugher?

indicators.note: the laugh is placed around the yearning, so these two letters sit about it

parts.words: What would be funny, doubling up
parts.note: HA is the laugh of someone doubled up at something funny
to long for something is to have a yen for it

explanation.surface: A riddle about which creature would be amusing, bent over around some long-laughing beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long' looks like an adjective for the laugh, but here it is the verb to yearn, giving the noun for a yearning.
explanation.definitionFit: The spotted hyena is famous for its cackling call, so it is nicknamed the laughing animal.

clue.text: In Jersey Zoo, Durrell's set up something outstanding

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the run is read upwards, so backwards
the letters sit inside the run of words Jersey Zoo Durrell's

explanation.surface: Gerald Durrell founded Jersey Zoo, and the clue praises his establishment as something special.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters YZOOD run across 'Jersey Zoo Durrell's'; 'set up' turns them over.
explanation.definitionFit: Doozy is American slang for a remarkable example of something, good or bad.

clue.text: Group of fine women taking on an expert in fashion

indicators.note: the letters so far take on the next ones, adding them at the end

parts.note: G stands for Group, as in G7
fine means okay, OK

explanation.surface: A collection of excellent women recruits a style guru.
explanation.walkthrough: Gok Wan is a British TV fashion presenter, known for 'How to Look Good Naked'.
explanation.definitionFit: He is a stylist and television presenter who advises people on clothes and appearance.

clue.text: It's in keeping with the bride to be faithful, so we hear

definitions.text: It's in keeping with the bride to be

indicators.note: the phrase signals that the result is spoken, matching a word spelt differently

parts.note: faithful means true, and so is taken as written, giving TRUE SO to be said aloud

explanation.surface: A rumour that something suits a bride and means remaining loyal.
explanation.walkthrough: TRUE SO said aloud gives the French-derived word; 'so we hear' marks the sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A trousseau is the clothes and linen a woman collects ahead of her marriage, kept in readiness for the wedding.

clue.text: Columns, not books etc, probing physical scale

indicators.note: something probing is pushed into the scale, so these letters go inside

parts.note: the Mohs scale measures mineral hardness
no means not
lit is short for literature

explanation.surface: A survey of pillars, ignoring literature, that investigates bodily size.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mohs scale ranks minerals by scratch-hardness, from talc to diamond.
explanation.definitionFit: Monoliths are single great upright stones, pillar-like structures standing alone.

clue.text: One may be represented by MC

definitions.text: One may be represented by MC

parts.words: One may be represented by MC
parts.note: MC is master of ceremonies, who presents a show; also MC is the Roman numeral 1100, a great multitude

explanation.walkthrough: MC reads as the compere of an event, but in Roman numerals it is 1100, which is a large crowd as well.
explanation.definitionFit: A presenter of a show is its compere, and a vast number of people is a multitude, both senses of the word.

clue.text: Area's premium beer keeps rocketing

indicators.note: in a down clue, rocketing means going upward, so the whole is read backwards
the beer holds the number one inside it

parts.note: lager is a beer
the premium item is number one, written NO I

explanation.surface: A locality's top ale keeps soaring in popularity.
explanation.walkthrough: LAGER holding NO I gives LANOIGER, which 'rocketing' turns upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Something regional belongs to a particular district, so it is the possessive of that district.

clue.text: See 1
Did swine and duck as tattoos

parts.note: a duck is a zero score in cricket, the letter O
tattooed skin is inked

explanation.surface: Pigs and ducks getting tattooed together.
explanation.walkthrough: Duck is cricket's word for a score of nought, hence O.
explanation.definitionFit: Oinking is the grunting noise pigs make, so this is what pigs did.

clue.text: Reversing roles (not mine, not indelicate), prepare for a difficult passage

indicators.note: the word for roles is turned around, read back to front

parts.note: roles are parts in a play
not mine means yours
elfin means dainty, delicate, the opposite of indelicate

explanation.surface: An actor swapping roles, avoiding his own and anything crude, braces for a rough journey.
explanation.walkthrough: Elfin describes small, dainty features, the opposite of indelicate.
explanation.definitionFit: Fastening your seatbelt before turbulence is the idiom for bracing yourself for a bumpy ride ahead.

clue.text: Pretty dim, it leaving Red Sea port without cargo

indicators.note: the word it departs from the darkness word

parts.note: a pretty dim place is unlit
Aden is a port in Yemen near the Red Sea

explanation.surface: A gloomy ship departs a Yemeni harbour with an empty hold.
explanation.walkthrough: UNLIT with 'leaving' removing IT gives UNL.
explanation.definitionFit: An unladen vessel or vehicle is carrying no load or freight.

clue.text: Album compilation some current prayer parts defraud

indicators.note: the swindle word is split apart so the other pieces go between its letters

parts.note: to sting is to swindle
an amp is a unit of electric current
a collect is a short liturgical prayer

explanation.surface: Bits of an electrical prayer, oddly, cheat people.
explanation.walkthrough: A collect is a short set prayer in Anglican and Catholic services; 'Album' points to the hobby, not a record.
explanation.definitionFit: Philately is the hobby of gathering postage stamps, typically arranged in an album.

clue.text: Heartless person bringing misery aboard conveyance equipped with rack?

definitions.text: Heartless person bringing misery aboard conveyance equipped with rack?

indicators.note: the remains of the scoundrel ride aboard the car, placed inside

parts.note: a tourer is a touring car, often with a roof rack

indicators.note: the middle letter of the scoundrel word is removed, as if its heart were cut out

parts.note: a rat is a nasty person who makes others wretched

explanation.surface: A cruel villain riding in a car with a luggage rack.
explanation.walkthrough: The rack is both a car's roof rack and the medieval stretching device, so the whole clue also defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who inflicts pain for cruelty and uses the rack as a device is exactly a pitiless inflicter of agony.

clue.text: Incarcerating drunk men in a terrible state

indicators.note: the jumbled letters lock the drunkard inside them
the words men in a are in a terrible mess, so reshuffled

parts.note: a sot is a drunkard

explanation.surface: Locking up the drunks, the men are in a dreadful condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges MEN IN A to MINNEA, and 'Incarcerating' puts SOT inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Minnesota is one of the fifty United States, in the upper Midwest.

clue.text: Unusual putting game ahead of the Barking Hotel?

definitions.text: Unusual putting game ahead of the Barking Hotel?

parts.words: Unusual putting game ahead of the Barking Hotel?
parts.note: in the NATO phonetic alphabet the letter word for G comes just before the one for H; crazy and barking both mean mad

explanation.walkthrough: Barking is British slang for mad, and in the radio alphabet Golf precedes Hotel, so a mad Golf comes before a barking Hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the miniature putting game with windmills and obstacles, found at seaside resorts.

clue.text: Robber we hear not after ships, securing new way to raise funds

indicators.note: the bandit holds the new letter inside him

parts.note: a brigand is a bandit

indicators.note: says the phrase is spoken, giving a sound-alike spelt differently

parts.note: by means not after, as in by noon, and ships travel by sail

explanation.surface: A sound like a pirate who travels before the fleet, seizing a new method of fundraising.
explanation.walkthrough: By means no later than; BY SAILS said aloud gives BUY SALE.
explanation.definitionFit: A bring-and-buy sale is a charity event where people donate goods and purchase others, raising money.

clue.text: Just underplays cryptic hint

indicators.note: cryptic means obscure, so the word underplays is scrambled

parts.note: to hint is to imply

explanation.surface: A puzzle setter merely understates a puzzling clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' looks like an adverb meaning fairly; it means merely.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean merely, nothing more, as in 'it was just a mistake'.

clue.text: Something in the sea salt I almost forgot to write about

indicators.note: the pieces are turned about, read backwards

parts.note: an old salt is a sailor, as is a tar
PS, postscript, is what you add when you nearly forgot to write something

explanation.surface: A seafarer adds an afterthought to his letter about the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns TARPS into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The sprat is a small oily marine fish of the herring family.

clue.text: A plumber, "Iron Man", repeatedly cut off supply

indicators.note: read as supple, bendy, so the remaining letters are rearranged
both the letters N of Iron Man are cut away, more than once

explanation.surface: A tradesman and a superhero both shut off a water supply.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing both Ns from IRONMAN leaves IROMA, which 'supply' (as in suppl-y, in a supple way) rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Mario is the Nintendo video-game character, an Italian-American plumber.

clue.text: Witness live projection

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look, behold
to be is to exist, to live

explanation.surface: A witness gives evidence through a live video projection.
explanation.walkthrough: Lo is the archaic call to look at something.
explanation.definitionFit: A lobe is a rounded part that sticks out, such as an earlobe.

clue.text: Arrange to take Doodlebug back over again?

indicators.note: the arranging word takes in the other letters

parts.note: to do a room is to arrange it

indicators.note: the bomb's name is read back to front

parts.note: the doodlebug was the German V-1 flying bomb, written V ONE

explanation.surface: Organising for a wartime flying bomb to come back again.
explanation.walkthrough: Doodlebug was the British wartime nickname for the V-1 flying bomb; 'back' turns V ONE into ENOV.
explanation.definitionFit: De novo is a Latin phrase meaning from the beginning, afresh, once more.

clue.text: In case of which pap makes unscheduled appearance?

definitions.text: In case of which pap makes unscheduled appearance?

parts.words: In case of which pap makes unscheduled appearance?
parts.note: pap is an old word for a nipple, and a case for clothes is the other sense of the first word

explanation.walkthrough: Pap suggests the paparazzi or baby food, but it is an old word for a nipple; 'In case of' hides the clothes cupboard.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the euphemism for an accidental exposure caused by clothing failing, made famous at the 2004 Super Bowl.
